root_idea.summary: The root centers on a voiced cry or call, especially a call used to summon someone.
root_idea.development: The primary notion of crying out develops into calling or summoning, including the Quranic imperative expression هَيْتَ لَكَ meaning “Come!” and related formations denoting repeated or clamorous calling.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Quranic expression هَيْتَ, whose lexical identity is supported directly by the supplied Quran-focused and Classical evidence.

senses.definition: A call meaning “Come!”, “come forward!”, “hasten!”, or “set forth.”
senses.usage_conditions: An invariable imperative expression, commonly followed by لَكَ or another pronoun marking the addressee; the expression itself does not vary for gender or number. It occurs in the Quran as هَيْتَ لَكَ.

senses.definition: In هَيْتَ لَكَ, an invitation meaning “I have made myself ready for you.”
senses.usage_conditions: This is the Quran-specific interpretation of the utterance in 12:23, expressing the speaker’s readiness to the addressee rather than merely issuing a neutral summons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cry out to, call, or hail someone, including a repeated call used by a herdsman to summon a companion from afar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II verbal construction; the calling expression may be repeated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Give me; hand or give something to me.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An imperative form whose inflection varies with the addressee in the recorded forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exclamation of wonder or admiration, as in “What forbearing mildness!”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An exclamatory use distinct from the summons هَيْتَ لَكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A low or depressed piece of ground; a hollow or depression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal geographical or topographical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clamorous; calling out often or repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive usage associated with frequent calling out.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form II calling construction is represented under its Classical meaning.
The imperative meaning “give me” is represented separately.
The exclamation of wonder is represented as a distinct Classical use.

cautions: The Quranic item is variously analyzed in the lexical tradition as an imperative expression or an invariable verbal noun, with variant vocalizations and readings; the public form follows the supplied QAC occurrence هَيْتَ.
